digest.component_or_area: completion verification and ticket store access
propositions: Full ticket-store materialization consumes 135-235 seconds across 5,500 directories and 132,000 files; scoped pinned-view extraction completes in ~29 milliseconds, approximately 4,600-8,000 times faster.
Pinned reads at a captured commit OID remain byte-identical while concurrent mutations advance the live store to a new OID, enabling read-only snapshot stability with ongoing live writes.
Exact ticket edits, newly created children, and global-context changes (e.g. .bridge_state/bindings.json) invalidate recorded read dependencies; unrelated mutations do not.
Isolated single-ticket reduction retains unresolved aliases, while full-store reduction with sibling context resolves them; scoped views require explicit resolver context to achieve canonical parity.
Current rebar close/signature workflow writes COMPLETION_VERDICT, STATUS, and SIGNATURE across multiple separate transactions outside a unified lock, permitting interleaving and incomplete artifacts.

Completion receipts must track exact ticket state, direct children, transitive descendants, relations, global inputs, and negative-existence reads; current validity checks omit child status, certificates, and hierarchy changes.
